title: Simple Establishment of a Vascularized Osteogenic Bone Marrow Niche Using Pre-Cast Poly(ethylene Glycol) (PEG) Hydrogels in an Imaging Microplate
protocol: Prepare the hBM-MSC cell suspension.
Grow hBM-MSCs to a confluence level of 70%-90% in MEMα supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 5 ng/mL FGF-2 in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Wash the cells with PBS.
Detach the cells using 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA for 3-5 min at 37 °C.
Stop the detachment process by flushing with basal medium (MEMα supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin).
Collect the suspended cells in a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Count the cells using a hematocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Determine the total number of cells in the suspension.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 200 x g for 5 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in an appropriate volume of basal medium to achieve a concentration of 1 x 10^7 cells/mL of stock solution.

Prepare 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes containing the required volume of basal medium supplemented with the respective growth factors (FGF-2 and BMP-2 at defined concentrations, e.g., 0 ng/mL, 25 ng/mL, 50 ng/mL, 100 ng/mL, or 200 ng/mL).
If cell seeding is to be performed using an automated liquid handler, consider the dead volume of the instrument.
For manual cell seeding, use a volume excess of 10%.
Dilute hBM-MSCs from the stock solution at a ratio of 1:66.67 to achieve a concentration of 1.5 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Prepare the plate for seeding by removing the polypropylene adhesive film covering the 96-well hydrogel plate.

Aspirate the storage buffer covering the hydrogels using a microplate washer or manually, positioning the tip against the wall and moving down toward the edge of the inner well while aspirating to avoid damaging the hydrogel surface.
Add 200 µL/well of the cell suspension after thoroughly mixing to ensure homogenous distribution of cells.
Avoid tilting the plate during seeding to prevent uneven sedimentation of cells in one region of the substrate.
Periodically mix the cell suspension manually (after seeding three wells) to maintain a homogeneous mixture.
Mix the cell suspension immediately before dispensing for automated seeding with a serological pipet.
Maintain cultures at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in a humidified atmosphere.
Monitor culture development by bright-field microscopy with a 5x objective as desired.
Acquire reference images approximately 30 min after seeding to evaluate the number of cells added.
Prepare flasks for HUVEC culture by coating with a solution consisting of 150 µg/mL rat-tail collagen I in 0.02 M acetic acid for 30 min at 37 °C.
Rinse coated flasks once with PBS before use.
Grow GFP-HUVECs to a confluence level of 80%-100% in EGM-2 supplemented with 10% FBS in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in a humidified atmosphere.
Use cells up to passage 7 for the experiment.
Wash GFP-HUVECs with PBS before detachment.
Detach cells using 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA for 2-3 min at 37 °C.
Stop the detachment process by flushing with basal medium (MEMα supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin).
Collect detached cells in a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Count cells using a hematocytometer or an automated cell counter to determine total number of cells present in the suspension.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 200 x g for 5 min.
Carefully remove supernatant from the pellet.
Resuspend cells in basal medium to achieve a concentration of 1 x 10^7 cells/mL of stock solution.
Prepare 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes containing basal medium supplemented with defined concentrations of FGF-2 and BMP-2.
Add GFP-HUVECs from the stock solution at a dilution of 1:66.67 to achieve a concentration of 1.5 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Aspirate the medium from the plate containing stromal monoculture.
Add 200 µL/well of the GFP-HUVEC cell suspension prepared in step 2.1.8.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in a humidified atmosphere.
Change the medium every 3-4 days.
Monitor the development of the culture by bright-field and fluorescence microscopy using a 5x objective as desired.
Maintain cultures until day 4 or day 7 for early or intermediate characterizations, respectively.
Pre-process all images acquired on the same day using Fiji.
Open all GFP channel images of the same time point in Fiji.
Open the Brightness & Contrast menu.
Select an image that represents an intermediate condition.
Auto-adjust the contrast by selecting Auto.
Select Set and check Propagate to all Other Open Images.
Visually assess if the automatically selected range fits all images of the current time point.
Manually re-adjust and re-propagate to all images as needed.
Save the adjusted images as TIF files.
Repeat pre-processing steps for other time points acquired.
Apply a median blur filter with a radius of 3 to all images.
Reduce image size by binning at a factor of 2x2.
Save pre-processed images as grayscale RGB Color TIF files in a folder for quantification.
Analyze all images in the folder using Batch Process mode in the Angiogenesis Analyzer for ImageJ.
Examine overlays of recognized structures and original images to validate results.
Adjust pre-processing parameters or exclude problematic areas if artificial structures are recognized.
Normalize obtained values to an area of 1 mm² by multiplying sample values by the ratio of analyzed area to 1 mm².
Extract various network parameters from the analysis to characterize the endothelial network.
Assess ECM deposition using immunofluorescence at desired end time points.
Wash cultures once with 200 µL/well of PBS for 5 min at room temperature (RT).
Fix cultures with 100 µL/well of 4% paraformaldehyde under a chemical fume hood for 30 min at RT.
Wash fixed cultures three times with 200 µL/well of PBS at RT, each time for 5 min.
Store fixed cultures at 4 °C in 200 µL/well of PBS or proceed to the next step immediately.
Incubate fixed cultures with 200 µL/well of 1% BSA in PBS as a blocking solution for 30 min at RT.
Aspirate the blocking solution.
Incubate with 100 µL/well of primary antibody solution in 1% BSA in PBS overnight at 4 °C.
Wash cultures three times with 200 µL/well of PBS at RT, each time for 5 min and at least once for 3 h.
Permeabilize the cultures using 0.3% Triton X-100 and 1% BSA in PBS for 30-90 min at RT, depending on the cellular density of the cultures.
Prepare staining buffer consisting of 0.1% Triton X-100, 1% BSA in PBS, and counterstains (e.g., 1 µg/mL DAPI and 1:4,000 phalloidin-rhodamine).
Add 100 μL/well of secondary staining solution.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Wash with 200 μl/well of PBS three times for 5 min each, at least once for 3 h and once for 5 min, respectively, at RT.
Acquire confocal stacks starting at the glass bottom with a z-step of 2.5 µm reaching a final height of 500 µm using a 10x objective and a 0.75x digital zoom.
Threshold each channel separately in Fiji before creating a composite for 3D reconstruction.
Generate the 3D reconstruction using Fiji 3D Viewer.
Acquire confocal stacks with a height of 100 µm, z-step of 5 µm, 10x objective, and 1.5x digital zoom for immunostainings.
Adjust brightness and contrast for each channel separately in Fiji before creating a composite.
Add 200 μL/well of Picrosirius Red staining solution to paraformaldehyde-fixed wells.
Incubate the wells with Picrosirius Red staining solution for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the stained wells five times with distilled water.
Wash the wells twice every day or every second day for 3-4 days while monitoring sample color clearing.
Keep the plates at 4°C during long washing steps exceeding 6 hours.
Acquire images of the stained samples using a bright-field microscope equipped with a color camera.
Maintain an equal white balance across all conditions.
Use low magnification (e.g., 2.5x) to scan the entire well for overviews of the samples.
Manually stitch images if automated stitching is not available in the software.
Follow steps described for Picrosirius Red staining to perform Alizarin Red staining, washing, and imaging.
Quantitatively assess ALP activity at different culture end time points using BCIP/NBT staining.
Wash cultures once with 200 µL/well of PBS.
Incubate cultures with BCIP/NBT substrate solution at 37°C while monitoring color development.
Wash cultures once with 200 µL/well of PBS upon color development.
Fix cultures with 4% paraformaldehyde as described in step 4.1.1.
Acquire color images of stained samples as described in step 4.2.3 for Picrosirius Red staining.
Quantify ALP activity in cell lysates at different culture end time points (e.g., day 4 and day 7 of co-culture).
Wash cultures three times with 200 µL/well of PBS before incubating with 200 µL/well of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA at 37°C.
Agitate cultures vigorously by pipetting up and down every 10 minutes to facilitate digestion, monitoring culture morphology under a standard cell culture microscope.
Transfer samples to 2 mL tubes upon obtaining a liquid, single-cell suspension with no elongated cellular structures (typically after 20-30 min).
Add 200 µL of MSC basal medium to inhibit Trypsin and centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 min.
Decant supernatant and freeze pellets at −80 °C, or proceed directly to step 5.2.3.
Thaw the cell pellets obtained in step 5.2.2.
Incubate with 500 µL of lysis buffer for 30 min on ice.
Centrifuge at 16,100 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Keep the samples on ice.
Prepare ALP reagent consisting of 20 mM 4-Nitrophenyl phosphate disodium salt hexahydrate and 4 mM MgCl2 in lysis buffer.
Dispense 50 µL of cell lysate supernatant into the wells of a standard, transparent, tissue-culture 96-well plate in duplicates.
Add lysis buffer to two wells as blank controls.
With a multichannel pipette, add 50 µL/well of ALP reagent to the wells filled.
Briefly shake the plate.
Incubate at 37 °C for 10 min protected from light.
Stop the reaction by adding 100 µL/well of 1 M NaOH using a multichannel pipette.
Read the optical density at 410 nm using a plate reader.
Average the technical duplicates.
Subtract the average of the blank controls.
Perform DNA quantification to normalize ALP activity against total cell number.
Use a method based on fluorescence measurements or any compatible method for DNA quantification in cell lysates.
Prepare reagents and DNA standards using commercially available kits according to the manufacturers' instructions.
If samples were frozen, thaw them, centrifuge at 16,100 x g for 2 min at 4 °C, and place on ice.
Dispense 50 µL of the cell lysate supernatant into black 96-well plate in duplicates.
Freeze the samples at −20 °C or −80 °C if necessary.
Add DNA standards in duplicates.
With a multichannel pipette, add 50 µL of the DNA staining agent to each well.
Incubate according to manufacturer's instructions and read fluorescence intensity.
Determine conversion of measured intensity values to DNA concentrations using standard curve values.
Normalize ALP values by dividing them by respective DNA concentration of each sample.
Prepare fresh culture medium containing the same growth factors used for the respective cultures until that point.
Prepare a control solution consisting of the diluent of the compound of interest and sterile-filter it.
Add the compound of interest at the desired concentration and an equal volume of the control solution to the culture medium designated for the test and control conditions, respectively.
Aspirate the medium from the culture.
Add 200 µL/well of the medium freshly prepared in step 6.1.1.
Incubate for a time appropriate for the compound to be tested.
Monitor the culture development.
Characterize the endothelial networks as described in section 3.

Assess the effectiveness of the compound in inhibiting angiogenesis or ablating the pre-formed structures using the GFP images and the quantitative network parameters extracted from the analysis described in step 3.7.
Mix other cell types such as MDA-MB-231 or U2OS cancer cells into the cultures at day 4 of co-culture in fresh culture medium.
Label the cancer cells using a live dye according to the manufacturer's instructions for clear identification from GFP-labeled HUVECs and non-labeled hBM-MSCs.
Prepare a suspension of cancer cells at a concentration of 1.5 x 10^4 cells/mL in fresh culture medium containing previously used growth factors.
Monitor the development of the co-culture system and observe the localization of cancer cells as desired.
